correctness.rationale: Dual coalescing lineages prove the fixed-age covariance m^2+(1-m^2)P(T_n<=t), where T_n has rate-one jumps in each direction. The stationary Pareto equilibrium-age survival H(t) is 1-t/mu below tau0 and tau0^(alpha-1)t^(1-alpha)/alpha above, giving exact C_n=(1-m^2)E[H(T_n)]. Solving the walk Laplace recurrence yields q(s)^n; Mellin/Beta inversion gives 2n Gamma(2b)Gamma(n-b)/((n+b)Gamma(b)Gamma(n+b)) for n>b. Cauchy–Schwarz and the Poisson(2tau0) jump bound remove the short-age cutoff at superpolynomial relative precision, and the gamma ratio gives the sharp constant. Covariance summation proves threshold alpha=3/2 and weighted triangular sums prove all variance prefactors. For alpha<=1 age diverges in probability, finite dual lineages coalesce a.s., giving only finite-dimensional mixture. Independent calculations checked b=1 exact moment 2/(n^2-1) and stationary-age continuity; not a spatial asymptotic simulation or proof.

final_claim: For zero-temperature voter/Glauber dynamics on Z reset globally at Pareto renewal times to the same i.i.d. initial spin environment, the annealed stationary covariance C_n is asymptotic to (1-m^2)/alpha*(4*tau0)^(alpha-1)*Gamma(alpha-1/2)/sqrt(pi) times n^(-2(alpha-1)) for alpha>1; susceptibility is finite iff alpha>3/2 with the stated three block-average variance regimes. For alpha<=1 only a local weak long-time uniform-spin mixture is asserted.
limitations: Infinite one-dimensional zero-temperature voter chain, independent initial spins, common reset clock.
Susceptibility means equal-time connected spatial covariance sum, not thermodynamic field-response susceptibility; alpha<=1 claim only finite-dimensional weak limit.
